transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I came in because... I just keep steering clear of my own workshop out back. And, honestly, any family get-together where my brother-in-law might show up. It's been going on a while, and I'm just tired of planning my whole life around not running into those reminders.
Can you tell me more about why you avoid your workshop and family gatherings where your brother-in-law might be? What exactly are you worried might happen if you were to go there?

Well, it's not exactly that I'm worried something new is going to happen. It's more about what it brings up. 

If I go out to the shop, or if I have to look at him, it just... well, out of nowhere I'll see his hand with that heavy tool again. It's like a picture that just pops right into my head. It even happens when I'm nowhere near him, just going about my day, like when I'm shaving in the morning or working on a painting. And whenever that picture pops up, it still makes my chest tighten. I just stay away from him and the shop because I don't want to trigger those images.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of intrusive, distressing memories and avoidance behavior points specifically toward Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Other anxiety disorders (F40.00, F40.10, F40.20) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42.0) are less consistent with the trauma-related nature of the symptoms described.

inference_history.note: The patient describes avoidance behavior related to specific places and people, which suggests a possible anxiety or phobic disorder. Also considering obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42.0) and adjustment disorder with anxiety (F43.10) given the impact on daily planning and life interference.
